fact: 1923年1月11日，法国总理雷蒙·普恩加莱下令法军占领鲁尔，以强迫德国交付赔款。普恩加莱对记者说：「使鲁尔采矿业瘫痪可能给法国也带来困难，但德国损失更大，法国将表现出必要的忍耐力以智胜德国政府。」英国政府认定占领非法。到1923年底，占领成本侵蚀了法国财政，法郎大幅贬值。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Occupation of the Ruhr
sources.quote: After much deliberation, Poincaré decided to occupy the Ruhr on 11 January 1923 in order to exact the reparations. Poincaré knew that it would cost France as well as Germany and told reporters on 29 January 1923: Paralyzing the mining industry in the Ruhr may inflict hardships on France as well as Germany, but Germany is the greater loser and France will show the endurance necessary to outwit the German Government.

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, France Occupies the Ruhr
sources.quote: The occupation of the Ruhr also did serious damage to the French economy. It greatly increased the size of France's budget deficit and further debilitated the already weak French franc.

fact: 1923年11月，在法国政府无力按1920年公约减少法兰西银行垫款的消息曝光后，法郎遭遇投机性抛售。法郎对美元汇率从1923年10月底的约17法郎兑1美元跌至1924年3月11日的27法郎以上。1923年法国财政赤字达180亿法郎（其中重建支出仅115亿法郎）。

sources.title: IMF eLibrary, Fluctuating Exchange Rates in Countries with Relatively Stable Economies
sources.quote: Finally, in November 1923, after the revelation of the French Government's inability to face the obligation to reduce its advances from the Bank of France in accordance with the 1920 Convention, a wave of speculative selling of the franc started. The exchange rate of the franc plummeted from approximately F 17 per U.S. dollar at the end of October 1923 to more than F 27 on March 11, 1924.

sources.title: The Art of Central Banking（GIPE）
sources.quote: In 1923 there had been a budget deficit of 18 milliards, although the capital outlay on reconstruction had been only 11½ milliards.

fact: 1923年11月，普恩加莱同意任命一个国际委员会审查德国的实际支付能力，标志着法国在鲁尔问题上的立场开始松动。到1924年6月，新任法国总理赫里欧坚定承诺达成解决方案并尽快从鲁尔撤军。1924年8月16日道威斯委员会达成协议，9月1日签署，法国同意撤离鲁尔。

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, France Occupies the Ruhr
sources.quote: Poincaré finally acknowledged that the size and schedule of German payments would have to be modified. In November of 1923, he agreed to the appointment of an international commission to examine the practical question of Germany's ability to pay. By June of 1924, the new French premier, Édouard Herriot, was firmly committed to reaching a settlement and withdrawing troops from the Ruhr district as soon as possible.

fact: 1923年法郎持续贬值：对美元从1922年5月的约9美分跌到1923年12月的约5美分，1924年3月进一步跌到3.5美分。法郎对英镑从战前的25.22跌到1924年初的122（后经干预回升到63）。物价随法郎贬值同步上涨。

sources.title: The Art of Central Banking（GIPE）
sources.quote: Meanwhile the franc had depreciated from 9 cents in May, 1922, to 5 cents in December, 1923. An ominous development was the failure of a loan issued by the Crédit National in January, 1924, which produced only 1636 millions in place of the 3 milliards required. The foreign exchange market became demoralised, and the franc fell in March, 1924, to 3½ cents.

sources.title: Paris School of Economics, Threat of a capital levy, expected devaluation and interest rates in France during the interwar period
sources.quote: A first exchange-rate crisis occurred in 1923-1924 when Poincaré sent the French army to the Ruhr region without obtaining much in the way of payments from Germany. A substantial increase in taxation and an international loan were necessary to bring the franc back from 122 to 63 to a pound (the prewar level being 25.22).

fact: 1924年3月，普恩加莱推动议会对几乎所有现行税收加征20%的「双倍附加税」（double décime），以填补财政赤字。同时以法兰西银行部分黄金储备为抵押，通过摩根公司从美国借款1亿美元、通过拉扎德公司从英国借款400万英镑，用于稳定法郎汇率。

sources.title: The Art of Central Banking（GIPE）
sources.quote: Clearly further taxation was imperative, and M. Poincaré obtained the imposition of a double décime, an addition of 20 per cent. to nearly all the existing taxes. At the same time he had recourse to external borrowing. ... credits were raised in America of $100,000,000 through Morgans, and in England of £4,000,000 through Lazards, by pledging a part of the gold reserve of the Bank of France.

sources.title: Minneapolis Fed, Some Neglected Monetary Aspects of the Poincaré Stabilization of 1926
sources.quote: From September 1923 to February 1924 the franc fell from 6.2 cents to 3.8 cents (almost 40 percent). Poincaré got Parliament to raise taxes (the so-called double decime tax). On the basis of the tax increase France also borrowed $100 million from Morgan and £4.0 million from Lazard-Preres.

fact: 1923年法国国家信用银行（Crédit National）1月发行的债券仅募得16.36亿法郎，远低于所需的30亿法郎。60亿法郎左右的国防票据和国库票据中，每月有70—80亿法郎到期需要续借。短期债务结构使政府信用极易受到债权人拒绝续借的攻击。1923年财政赤字180亿法郎。

sources.title: The Art of Central Banking（GIPE）
sources.quote: An ominous development was the failure of a loan issued by the Crédit National in January, 1924, which produced only 1636 millions in place of the 3 milliards required. ... Of the 60 milliards or so of National Defence notes and Treasury notes 7 or 8 milliards fell due every month. The immediate consequence of any distrust of the franc was a difficulty in renewing them.

sources.title: Paris School of Economics, Threat of a capital levy, expected devaluation and interest rates in France during the interwar period
sources.quote: the real danger lay in the floating debt. Of the 60 milliards or so of National Defence notes and Treasury notes 7 or 8 milliards fell due every month. The immediate consequence of any distrust of the franc was a difficulty in renewing them.

fact: 历史学家莎莉·马克斯认为鲁尔占领在经济上是有利可图的：扣除占领成本后，鲁尔与莱茵兰的占领收益接近9亿金马克。但这一收益被法郎贬值和占领的财政成本部分抵消。1919年至1925年法国发行了价值440亿法郎的债券用于重建受灾地区。

sources.title: Wikiwand，雷蒙·普恩加莱
sources.quote: 歷史學者莎莉·馬克斯認為,此舉是有利可圖的,既未導致德國的惡性通貨膨脹,也非1924年法郎崩潰的主因,扣除佔領成本後,魯爾與萊茵蘭的佔領收益接近9億金馬克。

sources.title: Britannica, A fragile stability 1922–29
sources.quote: The French government, by contrast, issued bonds worth 44,000,000,000 francs from 1919 to 1925 to finance reconstruction of its devastated regions.

fact: 鲁尔占领期间，法国的钢铁生产依赖德国煤炭供应。德国消极抵抗导致鲁尔煤炭外运量低于占领前水平，德国还停止进口铁矿石，造成法国洛林铁矿地区的重大财务损失。法国最终被迫增派5个师（7.5万部队）以及数千名行政人员、工程师和铁路工人来维持占领区运转。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Occupation of the Ruhr
sources.quote: Coal taken out of the Ruhr dropped to less than the French had been receiving previous to the occupation. The Germans also stopped importing iron ore, which caused significant financial losses in the French iron mining region of Lorraine.

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, France Occupies the Ruhr
sources.quote: In order to keep the shipments flowing, Poincaré was forced to send five army divisions (amounting to seventy-five thousand troops), as well as thousands of administrators, engineers, and railway workers.
